## About

AI-produced work on the complex structure on the six-sphere: workbench, course CG-S6, consolidation and the survey of 12 Nov 2026

# S6 complex-structure workbench

This repository holds the AI-produced work on the complex structure on the six-sphere S^6 and the material around it: the first check of the original manuscript, the workbench that grew from it (24 August to 9 September 2026), the course CG-S6 (to 11 October 2026), the consolidation of 30 September 2026, and a survey of all of it written on 12 November 2026. It was split out of yang-mills-interacting-workbench, whose `s6/` folder is copied here.

The construction itself is not ours. It is the 108-page manuscript produced with Claude under Levent Alpöge's direction ([AC26], https://alpo.ge/s6.pdf), and Philip Engel gave an independent treatment ([E26], arXiv:2609.38442). Neither document is reproduced here; see "What was left out".

## Status of the mathematics

Every proof in this repository was produced by AI models and has been reviewed only by other AI sessions, unless a file says otherwise. No proof here has been checked by a human mathematician. The labels "verified", "proved" or "closed" inside the files are the workbench's own; the workbench corrected its own "verified" proofs at least six times. The survey of 12 November (`survey_20261112/FINDINGS.md`) gives the status of each result, what it adds over [AC26], [E26] and later papers, and what a full check would have to establish.

## Where to start

  1. The survey of 12 November 2026: `survey_20261112/FINDINGS.md`. It ranks 32 findings, marks each as settled in the literature, proved in the workbench, sketch or open, and says where each statement and proof is. The readers' notes behind it are in `survey_20261112/work/*_notes.md`; their combined text is `survey_20261112/READING_NOTES.md`.
  2. The course CG-S6: `codex_workspace/courses/CG-S6/README.md`. Eleven lessons with companion chapters (HTML, with editable Markdown sources in `src/` and check scripts in `checks/`). It is the latest treatment of the construction, its topology, canonical ring, deformation and the Campana-Demailly-Peternell step.
  3. The canonical snapshot of early September 2026: `codex_workspace/canonical_S6_snapshot/`. Start with `workbench.pdf` (source `workbench.tex`) and `workbench_and_manuscript_overview.pdf`; the research files are in `supporting_materials/workbench/research/`, and the AI reviews of the manuscript in `supporting_materials/peer_reviews/` (map: `peer_reviews/README.md`).


## How the repository is organized

`codex_workspace/mathematical_consolidation/`  | The consolidation of 30 September 2026: `CONSOLIDATION.tex`, `CLAIM_LEDGER.md`, `MASTER_MAP.md`, mathematical checks, the catalogue build scripts and receipts  | Local Codex workspace
`codex_workspace/ledgers/`  | Source-reading ledgers and the index of source files  | Local Codex workspace

Links inside the copied folders keep their original form. Links in `yang_mills_repository_s6/` that point above the folder (`../`) refer to the Yang-Mills repository; absolute local paths refer to the machine where the work was done.

## Who produced what

All dates are 2026. Model names and effort settings are those given in the records named.

  * Original manuscript [AC26]: produced with Claude under Levent Alpöge's direction (credit as given in `codex_workspace/courses/CG-S6/provenance.json`). Not included.
  * Transcription of the manuscript and reviews A and B (24-26 August): ChatGPT in Pro mode (ten transcription strips, two full reviews and their corrective rounds). The build script of review B names the model as "OpenAI GPT-5.6 Pro" (`peer_reviews/reviewer_B_corrective_2026-08-25/source_record/scripts/build_reports.sh`); the files of review A do not name a model.
  * Review C and the workbench (24 August to 9 September): OpenAI Codex. According to the session records summarized in `survey_20261112/READING_NOTES.md` (reader I), the sub-agents were GPT-5.6 Sol at effort ultra until 4 September (with a few GPT-5.6 Luna and GPT-5.6 Terra sessions) and GPT-6 Astra at effort ultra from 5 September; the root session was recorded as GPT-6 Astra at effort ultra at the time of capture. The correction note [N] records "OpenAI Codex gpt-5.6-sol, Ultra".
  * Consolidation of 30 September and the custody records: OpenAI Codex; the consolidation main session is recorded as gpt-6-sol at effort ultra (`codex_workspace/custody/FINAL_CUSTODY_AUDIT.json`).
  * Course CG-S6 (to 11 October): OpenAI Codex, GPT-6 Astra at effort ultra (course README); prerequisite chapters keep GPT-6.1 Sol (reasoning effort ultra) authorship where their arguments are retained.
  * Paper [R], "The S6 record and the integral monodromy of its (3,4,∞) period system" (28 September), cited by the status note of 5 October: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max (the user's default then). Not in this repository.
  * Survey of 12 November (`survey_20261112/`): Claude Fable 5.2 at effort high, from its own reading and the notes of fifteen readers, also Claude Fable 5.2 at effort high. The survey is not a verification.
  * Returns of the Pro prompts (`pro_returns/`): GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), from 12 November; not reviewed by a person. The return notes and their filing: Claude Opus 5.5.
  * This repository's selection, privacy pass and README: Claude Opus 5.5.

## What was left out

`LEFT_OUT.tsv` lists every omitted file with the reason. In short:

  * copies of the original manuscript [AC26] (transcriptions, annotated copies, page extracts) and of third-party papers; the review reports themselves are included;
  * raw conversation material: Codex thread records, dialogue files and their extracts, including the 385 MB thread item ledger. The sanitized public records prepared for publication are included (`canonical_S6_snapshot/supporting_materials/publication/complete_sanitized_conversation_v1.jsonl` and `full_record_public_annex_v2/`);
  * the hash-named blob stores of the source archives (older versions of the files included here, mixed with conversation records and third-party papers), the private catalogue databases (270 MB) and private working copies;
  * the five related source tasks on other topics (Yang-Mills, Navier-Stokes, Riemann hypothesis, Geometric Unity);
  * TeX build by-products, Python caches, compiled binaries, rendered page images, the 77 MB Koide census (reproducible with the checker beside it) and duplicates.

The prompts for GPT-6 Astra in ChatGPT Pro mode that the survey prepared (six in `FINDINGS.md`, since merged into five: `S6_01_INVARIANTS`, `S6_02_FAMILY`, `S6_03_CDP`, `S6_04_MAPS_MANIFOLDS`, `S6_05_ARITHMETIC`) are published with their returns in `pro_returns/` as each comes back (see "Returns of the Pro prompts" below); the prompts' background archives (the attached sources) are not published.

## Returns of the Pro prompts

### S6_01_INVARIANTS (returned 12 November 2026)

AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode); not reviewed by a person. Folder: `pro_returns/S6_01_INVARIANTS/` (prompt `PROMPT.md`, notes `RETURN_NOTES.md`, the return unchanged in `return/`; check it there with `sha256sum -c MANIFEST_SHA256.txt`). The programs were returned by the model and have not been run by us. The model rendered pages 5, 62, 63 and 81 of [AC26] and extracted the text of pages 62-63 to check the passages it corrects. Those five files (`return/outputs/a_AC26_p5.png`, `a_AC26_p81.png`, `c_AC26_pages62_63.txt`, `return/logs/c_source-062.png`, `c_source-063.png`) are left out, because they reproduce pages of [AC26], which is not republished here; read the pages in the manuscript at https://alpo.ge/s6.pdf. They are listed in `LEFT_OUT.tsv` and in `RETURN_NOTES.md`. The return's own `MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` still lists them, so the check reports these five as missing and the other 110 files as matching.

What was asked. An independent derivation of the Hodge diamond of the complex threefold X of [AC26] with the decisive scalar evaluated (Part A); the same invariants for the other members of the family (B); Frölicher, Bott-Chern and Aeppli cohomology and special metrics (C); the tangent cohomology, the Kuranishi space and every Picard twist (D); and the deformations and comb members (E).

What came back. A 48-page paper (`return/S6_01_INVARIANTS_paper.pdf`) with 47 numbered statements (41 Proved, 2 Known, 2 Refuted, 2 Open; `return/S6_01_INVARIANTS_results.csv`), the report `return/S6_01_INVARIANTS_report.md`, code, outputs and logs. Fourteen of the sixteen items are finished at outcome (a), C.3 and E.2 are unfinished:

  * A.1-A.4: the cotangent direct images; the scalar μ_s(0) = i·4√π/(3^{3/4}Γ(1/4)²), nonzero, computed to 100 digits by two methods; h^{1,2} = h^{2,1} = 1, h^{1,1} = h^{2,2} = 2, independent of c; the cusp-torsion assertions of [AC26] Remarks 1.3 and 9.21 corrected (statement A4.2, Refuted), the workbench's degree-one correction confirmed.
  * B.1-B.3: the same Hodge numbers for all admissible (3,4) twists and all coprime (3k,4l); K_X and the anticanonical ring for each (3k,4l); the universal covers of the members with finite fundamental group have h^{1,1} = h^{2,2} = n+1.
  * C.1-C.2: E₁ ≠ E₂ = E_∞ with the differentials on a named basis; Bott-Chern numbers (1,0,2,2,2,2,1) and Aeppli numbers (1,2,2,2,2,0,1) computed directly.
  * C.3, unfinished: the Bott-Chern algebra, the Picard map, the +12 sign, the non-Kähler degrees and the metric types (no balanced, SKT, astheno-Kähler or Chern-Ricci-flat metric; Gauduchon metrics exist) are proved; evaluated coefficients of the global representatives G, Q are missing.
  * D.1-D.4: h(T_X) = (1,1,1,0); the Kodaira-Spencer map of the family is an isomorphism; the Kuranishi space is a smooth line; the tangent cohomology of every twist T_X ⊗ M, with r = 1 for every nonintegral twist.
  * E.1: small deformations keep the elliptic fibration and algebraic dimension one.
  * E.2, unfinished: for the comb members h(T_{X_m}) = (2m+1, 8m+1, 6m+1, 0) is proved, which refutes the universal bound h⁰(T) ≤ 2 of [AC26] Remarks 1.2/9.26 and of HKP Corollary 1.3 (statement E2.4, Refuted); the Hodge-kernel splitting, the torsion support and the obstruction maps remain open.

### S6_02_FAMILY (returned 12 November 2026)

AI-produced by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode); reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic, effort high), not by a person. Folder: `pro_returns/S6_02_FAMILY/` (prompt `PROMPT.md`, notes `RETURN_NOTES.md`, the return unchanged in `return/` except one page render of [AC26], listed in `LEFT_OUT.tsv`); review in `reviews/S6_02_REVIEW_FABLE/`. The review finds 0 wrong of 55 statements. The classification of the (3,4) family up to biholomorphism (c' - c in 2Z), its Kuranishi space and Aut = C^* are known from version 1 of arXiv:2610.00250 (Du, Guo, Kusakabe, Xie); new as far as the searches go: the exact domain (radius 216 in w), the complete discrete invariants, the correction of Engel's Remark 8.1, the real structures, the closed formula for the missing period, the monodromy group and the answer to Klingler's question, and the fibre loci. Open: C.3, E.1, E.2.

### Prompts not yet returned, routes and a lattice question (13 November 2026)

  * `pro_returns/S6_02_PUSH/PROMPT.md`, `pro_returns/S6_03_CDP/PROMPT.md`, `pro_returns/S6_04_MAPS_MANIFOLDS/PROMPT.md` and `pro_returns/S6_05_ARITHMETIC/PROMPT.md`: the four prompts as they stand, written or revised on 12-13 November by Claude Fable 5.2 (at effort high in the S6_02 review of 12 November, at effort max on 13 November) after the review of S6_02_FAMILY. Each return will be filed in the same folder when it comes back. The background archives are not published.
  * `reviews/S6_ROUTES_FABLE_MAX/`: routes for three questions that had no named route (`ROUTES.md`, `NOTES.md`, numerical tests in `checks/`), by Claude Fable 5.2 (effort max). By its own statement it is an unverified hunch: nothing in it is proved.
  * `reviews/LEECH_Z24_QUESTION_20261113.md` and `reviews/LEECH_Z24_CONSULT_20261113.md`: the question whether H_2 of the boundary complex of the moduli space of stable 6-pointed curves of genus 0 (Z^24) is related to the Leech and Niemeier lattices, and the answer of the S6 survey agent (Claude Fable 5.2 at effort high), given by hand without programs. `tools/delta06_lattice_20261113.py` computes the cycle lattice of that complex and the S_6 character on it in exact integer arithmetic; its output is not included and nobody has checked it.

## Changes made for publication

The user's first name was replaced by "user" in every file, including local paths and the contents of compressed files. Files changed this way no longer match the SHA-256 values recorded for them in the manifests and receipts inside the copied folders. No other content was changed.

## Rights

The rights in the original manuscript [AC26] and in [E26] belong to their authors; neither is reproduced here. To the extent we hold rights in the AI-produced material of this repository, they are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. Bundled third-party software and fonts (for example MathJax in `codex_workspace/courses/CG-S6/assets/`) keep their own notices.

Claude's own mathematical notes (`claude_math_notes/`): the working notes of the main session (Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max) from 15 November 2026 on S6 and on the Grothendieck programme, with the consults they started and the scripts of their checks; raw provenance, not refereed. `PROGRAMS.md` says which sections are about S6.

### 1.5 Methodology

This text is AI-produced; no part of it was written by a human. GPT-5.6 Sol (OpenAI), in Codex at reasoning effort ultra, wrote a first working edition (24 August–9 September 2026). GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, carried out the research runs (12–16 November 2026), an independent run that re-derived the stated results without their proofs (16–18 November), and the writing runs (16–20 November). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort high and at effort max, and Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at effort max, read, checked and recomputed the results between the runs (12–20 November); what they found went into the next run. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max revised the presentation of this version on 20 November 2026, without changing the mathematics of the results.

Each statement was checked by targeted proof checks (every step derived before the printed step was read, then compared), by independent re-proofs, and by independent computations; the numerical constants rest on interval-arithmetic certificates. For the statements of this paper the check record contains 369 targeted proof checks, 53 independent re-proofs and 157 computations or formal certificates. No human has checked the mathematics.

The programs named in the proofs, their outputs, the records of the runs and the check record of every statement are in the repository s6-complex-structure-workbench, commit 83d76022bc, folder `pro_returns/S6_SERIES_GRIND_checkpoint_10_2026112010211Z`; the programs are in its folder `code`, and the check record of each statement is in `S6_SERIES_GRIND_checks_V.md` under its tag. We dedicate this text to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal.

### 1.6 How the paper is organized

Part I (Section 2) constructs the fibre-product fourfold of Theorem A. Part II constructs the rank-six family: the cusp and the finite fillings and the integral eight-manifold (Sections 3–5), the periods (Section 6), the diffeomorphism type (Section 7), the parameter domain (Section 8), cohomology, deformations and isomorphisms (Section 9), the boundary of the family (Section 10), the classification of the integral data (Section 11) and the existence of periods for every such datum (Section 12).
